newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Bre-X off in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Bre-X off in heavy trade.

text.p: Troubled Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd eased in heavy volume Wednesday to highlight trade in foreign shares and American Depositary Receipts ADRs.
Traders said ADR investors were avoiding risks ahead of Friday's release of U.S. payroll data. If the numbers indicate a rise in inflation, they could mean a further increase in U.S. interest rates.
"The trend is a little bit of uncertainty with the looming prospect of a Fed rate rise," a trader said. "Cautious is probably the name of the game."
Bre-X was off 1/16 to 2-15/16 in mid-afternoon. Volume was 8.2 million shares and the company was among the most active on the Nasdaq exchange and by far the mostly heavily traded foreign company.

Bre-X has been hit by allegations it overstated gold reserves at its Busang project in Indonesia. For the second consecutive day, trade in Bre-X was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange Wednesday morning because of technical problems.
Among other foreign companies, Swedish telephone equipment company LM Ericsson fell 1-1/4 to 32-1/4.

The ADRs were hurt by questions about Ericsson's financial links with the United States' Pocket Communications Inc, a wireless personal communications services operator that sought bankruptcy protection this week.
An Ericsson spokesman said the company was not financially exposed to Pocket and would not lose any money if it went bankrupt.

Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone holding Telebras rose 1-3/4 to 106-7/8 after Brazil's communications minister said 1997 revenues would be about 22 billion reais and gave details about the privatization of state telephone monopolies.
Decliners led advancers 342 to 181 among 806 ADRs. The ADR index was off 0.60 percent and volume was 52 million.
